document.title: uketsuke Initial Implementation Specification
document.purpose: Define the first dependable, FileTalk-based uketsuke package: receive job files, dispatch work, report outcomes, and retire the files.
author: Lion Kimbro
Codex
depends-on: filetalk concept in Lion's Dictionary for LLMs

overview.summary: uketsuke is a small Python package for use by another Python program. Its receptionist machine watches inbox/, accepts one request-file at a time, dispatches work on that file, writes a response describing the result, and reconciles the completed work into durable completed storage.
overview.name-meaning: uketsuke is treated as the receptionist at the front desk: it receives, routes, reports, and closes the record.
overview.initial-goal: Make one complete job lifecycle dependable and inspectable before adding richer routing, concurrency, or distributed coordination.
overview.abstract-protocol: A job is a file. The core protocol is defined in terms of file discovery, claiming, dispatch, response, and completion. The file's contents and extension are not fixed by this specification.
overview.example-representation: JSON is used for demonstrations, test fixtures, and example handlers only. JSON is not the abstract job protocol and is not required of job producers or handlers.
non-goals: A network service or socket-based broker.
A guarantee that arbitrary jobs are safe to execute.
A command-line application or invocation manager.

terminology.host-program: The Python application that imports uketsuke. It receives command-line arguments, owns the work being answered, owns or configures the inbox/, supplies folder locations and host callbacks, and uses uketsuke for dependable file lifecycle handling.
terminology.host-platform: The operating-system and filesystem environment in which the host-program and uketsuke run. It provides process execution, memory, directories, file movement, and durability or synchronization mechanisms.
terminology.request-file: The opaque file that arrives through inbox/. uketsuke manages its lifecycle but does not assume how its message information is encoded.
terminology.response-file: The JSON file written by uketsuke to report what happened to a request-file. Its JSON shape is part of the uketsuke contract and will be specified separately.
terminology.message-key: A named fact that the host-program knows how to extract from a request-file, such as MESSAGE_ID, EXECUTION_TIMEOUT, or RESPONSE_TIMEOUT.
terminology.get-key: The host-program-supplied function uketsuke calls as get_key(request_file, KEY) to obtain a message-key value. uketsuke does not know the extraction mechanism.
terminology.uketsuke: The importable receptionist package that owns the lifecycle machine and writes response-files.
terminology.handler: The host-program-supplied work operation selected for a claimed request-file.

platform-and-packaging.distribution: A Python package imported and used by Python programs.
platform-and-packaging.package-responsibility: Expose the receptionist and dispatch machinery as importable Python functionality.
platform-and-packaging.invocation: Outside the package boundary. uketsuke does not define or manage its own process invocation.
platform-and-packaging.harness: Testing and demonstration require a separate package under src/. A final package name is not yet chosen; src/test-uketsuke/ is a candidate name, subject to Python package naming rules.
platform-and-packaging.harness-responsibility: Create temporary inbox/work_space/claimed/work_space/response-pending/work_space/reply-sent/work_space/done environments, create example request-files, call uketsuke through its importable API, and inspect response-files.

design-principles: Filesystem is the transport boundary; no sockets or shared memory are required.
Request-files are abstract files; JSON is the fixed representation of response-files and an example representation for request-files in demonstrations and fixtures.
A job file is an inspectable durable artifact, not merely an in-memory queue item.
External file paths and file lifecycle state are normalized and checked at the castle gate before dispatch.
The trusted interior operates on canonical current-file state; file contents remain job-specific unless a handler chooses to interpret them.
Claiming a job is an atomic filesystem operation where the platform permits it.
Work is reported before it is marked completed.
Completion preserves a durable outcome record; the safeguarded working copy may be deleted after terminal completion.
The first runtime is single-process and sequential unless a later specification changes this explicitly.

message-boundary.purpose: Extract message information without making uketsuke depend on the request-file format.
message-boundary.rule: uketsuke may request named keys, but does not interpret the request-file directly.

filesystem-boundary.purpose: Supply low-level filesystem primitives and durability behavior without making uketsuke depend on one operating system implementation.
host-primitives: write a file and synchronize it to disk
other low-level operations may be added when required, such as moving or deleting a file; these do not transfer lifecycle ownership to the host
filesystem-boundary.rule: The host supplies primitive file access. uketsuke combines those primitives into the semantic lifecycle operations that define the receptionist.

filesystem-layout.root: The host-program supplies inbox/. uketsuke receives a work_space/ directory and has total authority over its contents.

directories.inbox/: Host-program-owned source directory for incoming request-files. It is outside uketsuke's work_space/ authority.
directories.work_space/: uketsuke-owned root for claimed files, state transitions, response records, completion records, and temporary files.
directories.work_space/claimed/: Claimed request-files awaiting characterization or execution.
directories.work_space/executing/: Request-files whose host-program execution is currently being attempted.
directories.work_space/response-pending/: Request-files with a durable execution outcome whose response still needs reconciliation.
directories.work_space/reply-sent/: Request-files whose response-file has been durably written and whose final completion move remains to be reconciled.
directories.work_space/done/: Terminal outcome records, including successful, failed, interrupted, and rejected outcomes as status projections. The safeguarded request-file may be deleted after the record is durable.
directories.work_space/dead-letter/: Request-files that cannot be safely interpreted, completed, or answered; never silently discarded.
directories.work_space/tmp/: Temporary files used while writing JSON or assembling an artifact; contents are not part of the public protocol.

file-naming.job: A deterministic safe filename chosen by the producer or configured convention.
file-naming.response: A deterministic safe filename associated with the claimed job file.
file-naming.completion-record: A lifecycle record associated with the completed request-file; representation is not prescribed.
file-naming.rule: Names must be deterministic where an association is required and must not permit path traversal.

lifecycle.host-loop: The host-program owns the main runtime loop and calls one uketsuke reconciliation turn at a time. uketsuke does not own invocation or the outer loop.
lifecycle.turn-function: The exact public function name is not fixed yet. Conceptually it is a reconcile/do-something operation that inspects the filesystem and performs at most one meaningful lifecycle action.
priority-order: If no response obligation needs work, find and execute one request-file.
If neither exists, report that there is no work to do.
response-reconciliation-turn: Inspect the filesystem for a completed task whose response has not been durably handled.
If a JSON response-file is missing or incomplete, create or finish it from the durable task outcome.
If the response-file is already present, treat it as evidence and reconcile without duplicating it.
If a response was requested and can be delivered, complete the response obligation.
If no response was requested, skip response publication while still recording completion.
After the response obligation is complete, atomically mark the request-file completed.
execution-turn: Inspect inbox/ for one request-file needing execution.
Claim it by moving it into work_space/claimed/.
Build the current job record and call characterize_job(job) when the execution history is uncertain.
If characterize_job(job) returns unknown, reject the job and do not attempt execution.
If characterize_job(job) returns do-not-retry, record an interrupted outcome and do not attempt execution.
If characterize_job(job) returns retry-safe, move the job into work_space/executing/ and attempt execution.
The host-program's execute_job(job) function interprets the request-file, selects the task, extracts parameters, and performs the work.
Catch task execution failures and convert them into a durable failure outcome.
Durably record the task outcome and move the request-file into work_space/response-pending/ or work_space/done/ as appropriate.
Return control to the host-program; response delivery is reconciled on a later turn.
invalid-input-flow: If a discovered request-file cannot be read or cannot provide enough information to construct a job record, move it to work_space/dead-letter/.
If characterize_job(job) returns unknown, move the job to work_space/done/ with rejected status or to work_space/dead-letter/ according to the final rejection policy.
A rejected request does not require a response; a response is written only if RESPONSE_ADDRESS can be obtained.
crash-recovery: A file in inbox/ is unclaimed and may be claimed.
A file in work_space/claimed/ may not yet have been attempted or may have been interrupted before execution began.
A file in work_space/executing/ may have been executing when the host-program stopped; characterization is required before another attempt.
A file in work_space/response-pending/ has a durable task outcome and must be reconciled before new execution.
A file in work_space/reply-sent/ has a durable response-file and needs only final completion reconciliation.
A file in work_space/done/ is not executed again by default.
Recovery must never overwrite an existing response-file or completion marker without an explicit reconciliation rule.

dispatch.model: uketsuke delegates request interpretation and task dispatch to one host-program function.
dispatch.selection: execute_job(job) selects the task, decodes the request-file, extracts parameters, and performs the work.
dispatch.handler-contract: execute_job(job) returns JSON-compatible response data on success or raises an exception on failure.
dispatch.initial-execution: Handlers run synchronously in the uketsuke process, one claimed job at a time.
dispatch.failure-capture: The execution boundary uses a broad exception capture around execute_job(job) so ordinary task failures become durable failure outcomes instead of escaping into the host-program's main loop. Process-control exceptions such as interruption or termination remain a separate policy decision.
dispatch.characterization-contract: characterize_job(job) returns exactly retry-safe, do-not-retry, or unknown. retry-safe permits another execution attempt; do-not-retry produces interrupted status without another attempt; unknown means the host cannot recognize the job and produces rejected status without another attempt.
dispatch.task-result: A successful task returns response data. A task with no response data still produces a successful completion outcome when the request asks for no response.
dispatch.unknown-selection: A request-file for which no task handler can be selected becomes a failure outcome; it receives a failure response only if a response address can be extracted.
dispatch.handler-boundary: The host's execute_job(job) function must not mutate inbox/ or any lifecycle directory beneath work_space/. The receptionist owns lifecycle movement and response publication.

runtime-job-record.description: The job is an internal Python dictionary owned by uketsuke. It is a live runtime record, not the request-file's message format and not a JSON wire object.

example.job-file: pathlib.Path('<full path beneath work_space/ while resolving>')

field-rules: message-id is obtained through get_key(); uketsuke does not decode it from the request-file.
inbox-filename preserves the original source filename for identity and diagnostics.
job-file points to uketsuke's safeguarded copy or current lifecycle location beneath work_space/ and may cease to exist after the terminal outcome record is durable.
response contains host-produced response data only after execute_job(job) succeeds.
error contains a JSON-safe diagnostic record or string, never a raw exception object.
The record may contain additional runtime-only fields as the implementation develops.

configuration.shape: One coherent configuration dictionary is supplied by the host-program.
configuration.tasks: No task registry is required in uketsuke. execute_job(job) owns message decoding, task selection, parameter extraction, and task execution.

ownership-of-file-operations.explanation: The host-program gives uketsuke the primitive ability to work with durable files. uketsuke owns the policy, ordering, naming, movement, and lifecycle meaning of inbox/ and every directory beneath work_space/.

operational-contract.execution-model: Reconciliation, not a single forward-only pipeline. Each host-program turn asks what durable obligation is unfinished and repairs one obligation before looking for new work.
operational-contract.polling: The host-program repeatedly asks the package for one reconciliation turn. Poll interval and host loop policy are outside uketsuke.
operational-contract.ordering: The initial implementation makes no global ordering promise. Within one scan, deterministic filename ordering is preferred.
operational-contract.identity: The job file's safe name or configured file identity is the initial identity candidate. A separate job-id field is not required by the abstract protocol.
operational-contract.delivery-order: Response reconciliation has priority over new task execution.
operational-contract.execution-delivery: Task execution is at-least-once across crashes unless a stronger task-specific mechanism is added.
operational-contract.idempotency: Tasks should be idempotent. A task that cannot safely be repeated requires an explicit task-specific protection or must be treated as potentially unsafe after interruption.
operational-contract.atomicity: All public artifacts are written to tmp/ and atomically renamed into their final directory; JSON is used only when the selected artifact representation is JSON.
operational-contract.logging: Operational logs are append-only JSONL where implemented; the response-file and completion record remain the authoritative per-request outcome artifacts.
operational-contract.observability: At every lifecycle boundary, the filesystem should make it possible to determine whether a request-file is received, claimed, executing, response-pending, completed, failed, or quarantined.

response-semantics.success: The handler completed and returned a result accepted by uketsuke.
response-semantics.failure: The request-file was accepted and dispatched, but the task or lifecycle operation failed. A failure response is written when a response address is available.
response-semantics.no-response: The request-file explicitly indicates that no response is wanted. uketsuke records completion without writing a response-file.
response-semantics.unreplyable: The request-file cannot yield a response address, so uketsuke cannot send a response. This is represented as durable failure/quarantine state, not a rejected response.
response-semantics.response-timing: The JSON response-file is published before normal completion is finalized.
response-semantics.result-preservation: The response-file contains a concise JSON envelope with success or failure status, response data when available, and diagnostics when appropriate. Handler runtime objects must be converted to JSON-compatible values before publication.

recommended-modules: paths: configured directories and safe filename construction
files: file discovery, safe movement, and atomic artifact writes
jobs: boundary normalization and file identity
dispatch: handler registration and current-file execution
receptionist: reconciliation, claiming, execution, reporting, and completion machine
configuration: caller-supplied directories and handler selection rules
implementation-shape.machine-state: The receptionist module should expose a small g bundle for run state and a register for the current job file. Internal lifecycle steps should be named zero-argument machine actions; arguments should represent caller-selected variation only.
implementation-shape.startup: No operational calls at import time. The importing host program configures and starts the package through its Python API.
implementation-shape.invocation-boundary: uketsuke does not own a main loop, CLI, service process, or invocation policy.
implementation-shape.test-and-demo-boundary: Harness code belongs in a separate src/<harness-package>/ package and may use JSON fixtures for demonstrations.
implementation-shape.classes: No classes are required for the initial implementation.

acceptance-criteria: A valid request-file placed into inbox/ is eventually claimed, dispatched, answered when appropriate, and completed.
A handler result produces a JSON response-file associated with the same request-file when a response is requested.
A handler exception produces a failure outcome and does not crash the host-program's main loop.
An unreadable or unacceptable job file is quarantined without dispatch and without silent deletion.
A partial public artifact is never treated as a complete incoming job.
A restart can distinguish inbox, claimed, executing, response-pending, reply-sent, done, and dead-letter states.
Repeated reconciliation does not ordinarily dispatch a completed request-file a second time.
Public artifact writes are atomic at the filesystem boundary; encoding is selected by the artifact representation.
The package is usable by an importing Python program without invoking a uketsuke-owned process.
A separate harness covers successful dispatch, missing handler selection, handler failure, unacceptable input, and recovery from interrupted lifecycle steps.
open-questions: How are handlers selected from a job file: filename convention, extension, sidecar metadata, directory, or file contents?
Should handlers be Python callables only, or may the host program adapt other executors?
What exact JSON fields and vocabulary belong in the response-file?
What exactly counts as a durably sent response-file, and what evidence should reconciliation use before moving from reply-sent/ to done/?
What operator action finalizes or replays a job stranded in working/?
What should the importing host program call to perform one scan or run a longer receptionist loop?
What retention policy governs completed/, failed/, and dead-letter/?
Do job producers require identity, correlation, priority, or retry metadata in v1?
What final importable package name should the separate test/demo harness use?

softspec.role: Non-normative JSON examples only. These structures demonstrate one possible representation and do not define the abstract job-file protocol.

job-id.description: Stable identity of one uketsuke job.
job-id.constraints: Non-empty safe identifier; must not contain path separators or traversal segments.

job-type.description: Registry key selecting the handler for a job.

timestamp.description: Creation or lifecycle time; exact representation remains an open question.

job.title: Uketsuke Job
job.description: One possible JSON representation of a job file for demonstrations. The abstract protocol does not require these fields.

payload.type: object or other JSON-compatible value selected by job-type

response.title: Uketsuke Job Response
response.description: One possible JSON representation of a response file for demonstrations. The abstract protocol does not require JSON.

completion-record.title: Uketsuke Completion Record
completion-record.description: One possible JSON representation of completion evidence for demonstrations. The abstract protocol does not require JSON.

notes: This is an initial implementation specification, not a complete FileTalk or workflow standard.
The inbox/ convention is specific to uketsuke and does not redefine FileTalk itself.
The specification intentionally leaves room for later job envelopes, subprocess handlers, retries, acknowledgements, and richer routing.
The abstract unit is a file. JSON appears below only as an example representation for tests and demonstrations.
The package is a Windows 11 Python library used by importing programs; invocation and the demonstration harness are outside the uketsuke package.
